page: Microsoft Azure F4als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at up to 4.5 GHz based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, mapping directly to 4 vCPUs. Cache allocation includes 48 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 8.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local instance storage, relying entirely on remote premium storage capabilities.

In benchmark evaluations, the high clock frequency of the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor delivers top-tier single-core performance. Single-threaded stress-ng operations reached 3,783.49, placing within the top decile of measured systems. Similarly, single-threaded data compression tasks show strong results, with gzip compression recording 40.46 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression achieving 18.11 GB/sec. Multi-core compute and PassMark CPU metrics align with mid-range tiers at 15,088.73 and 13,471.73 respectively. Memory bandwidth registers at 53.17 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 34.25 GB/sec for writes. The CPU supports advanced vector extensions including AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, facilitating accelerated execution for supported mathematical and light inference workloads.

The resource allocation profile of the F4als_v7 reflects a focused compute architecture suited for CPU-bound tasks that do not demand extensive RAM footprints. Because memory is constrained to 8.0 GB and local ephemeral disks are absent, it is not configured for large in-memory caching or heavy local I/O databases. However, dedicated non-hyperthreaded cores provide predictable execution times and resource efficiency for continuous processing. Suitable workloads include build automation, continuous integration pipelines, batch processing, static web serving, algorithmic computation, and front-end application logic.
description: Microsoft Azure F4als_v7 is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with an 8.0 GB memory footprint (2.0 GB per vCPU), the instance features a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio and lacks local scratch storage and dedicated GPU hardware, depending on networked premium storage. Benchmark results show exceptional single-threaded performance, with stress-ng and compression metrics placing in the top ten percent, alongside solid vector acceleration capabilities via AVX-512 and AVX-VNNI. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing speeds without hyperthreading contention. Given the memory constraints and lack of local NVMe disks, F4als_v7 represents a balanced, cost-effective resource for compute-intensive tasks, batch compilation, continuous integration pipelines, algorithmic jobs, and application serving that require high single-thread speeds without large in-memory working sets.
